name: Crucible Industries Storm Platform CP-8 'Deluge'
description:
A man-portable squad support weapon that fires caseless 6mm rounds from a 200-round helical magazine at 1,400 rounds per minute. The Storm Platform is Crucible's mainline suppression tool — designed to pin entire squads behind cover while assault elements maneuver.

The CP-8 uses a rotating barrel cluster of three barrels that cycle to manage heat distribution, allowing sustained fire for 8-second bursts without thermal degradation. The weapon feeds from a drum-style helical magazine worn on the operator's back, connected by an armored feed chute that allows full range of motion.

Crucible designed the Deluge to be the loudest thing in any engagement. The weapon's acoustic signature at full cyclic rate is physically disorienting to personnel within 30 meters of the firing position — a deliberate feature that Crucible calls 'ambient suppression.' You don't need to hit someone to suppress them when the sound alone triggers a primal fear response.
legality: Military restricted — squad support weapon authorization
specifications:
caliber: 6mm caseless
effective_range: 50-800 meters
rate_of_fire: 1,400 rounds per minute (cyclic)
capacity: 200-round helical drum
weight: 11.2 kg weapon, 4.8 kg loaded magazine
power_source: None — mechanical action
tactical_use: The Deluge is deployed as the centerpiece of squad-level fire-and-maneuver tactics. The weapon's extreme rate of fire and acoustic signature fix enemy positions, creating windows for assault teams to close distance. Operators learn to fire in controlled bursts that maintain the psychological pressure of sustained fire while conserving ammunition. In urban environments, the CP-8's penetration characteristics allow suppressive fire through light cover, denying concealment as well as movement.
cultural_context: The sound of a Deluge is one of the most recognized auditory signatures in GLMZ's conflict zones. Lower-tier residents who live near corporate borders describe it as 'the rain' — a hammering roar that signals active combat and the need to shelter. Crucible's marketing leans into the weather metaphor, with promotional materials declaring 'When it rains, nothing grows.'
story_hooks: A Deluge was recovered from a Tier 2 gang hideout — a weapon that should be impossible to obtain outside military channels. The serial number traces to a shipment that was reported destroyed in transit.
Crucible is testing a CP-8 variant with smart ammunition that adjusts trajectory mid-flight to avoid designated 'no-strike' zones — a response to mounting civilian casualty concerns.

physical_description.visual_profile: A brutalist support weapon with aggressive angular lines. The CP-8 presents as a compact, bullpup-oriented platform dominated by a distinctive rotating barrel cluster at the muzzle — three gleaming cylinders arranged in a triangular formation that dominate the front profile. The weapon has a wedge-like receiver with pronounced top rails and venting, giving it a predatory, heat-management aesthetic. At full profile, it reads as industrial and purposeful rather than sleek.
physical_description.dimensions: Overall length: 67 cm. Barrel cluster diameter: 4.2 cm. Width at receiver: 8.5 cm. Height with sights: 12 cm.
physical_description.weight_description: Dense and authoritative in the hand — 11.2 kg of weapon alone demands respect and core strength to manipulate. Balanced forward of the trigger group to manage rotational momentum of the barrel cluster. With backpack magazine system connected, the platform becomes a two-piece unit with distributed weight — heavy but not unwieldy for sustained suppressive fire.
physical_description.primary_material: Reinforced polymer composite receiver with steel barrel cluster and rotating breach housing. Feed chute and magazine coupling points are hardened steel. Buttstock incorporates shock-absorbing elastomer.
physical_description.finish: Matte graphite polymer with brushed steel barrel assembly. The barrel cluster shows visible heat-bluing from sustained fire cycles — intentional aesthetic that signals the weapon's thermal pedigree. Receiver rails have a anodized gunmetal finish with subtle grooving for equipment mounting.
physical_description.color_scheme: Charcoal gray polymer body with steel-silver barrel cluster. Accent trim in tactical orange on the charging handle and magazine coupling indicator.
physical_description.grip_texture: Rubberized pistol grip with aggressive stippling for wet-glove handling. Magazine housing grip (on backpack unit) uses softer elastomer for extended carry comfort. Fore-grip is wrapped in textured neoprene with beveled edges.
distinctive_features: Three-barrel rotating cluster with individual heat sinks machined into the shroud
Large spiral grooves on barrel housing for visual heat dissipation design language
Prominent feed chute with armored flex coupling connecting to backpack magazine
Charging handle positioned high and rearward, chrome-plated and oversized for gloved operation
Picatinny rail running full length of receiver with secondary rails on both sides
Thermal indicator stripe (color-shift paint) running along receiver — green at cold, yellow at warm, red at critical
Audible feedback port with acoustic amplification chamber beneath muzzle brake
Magazine coupling lock mechanism with redundant fail-safe indicators
physical_description.manufacturer_markings: CRUCIBLE INDUSTRIES stamped in angular sans-serif on the receiver left side. Model designation 'CP-8' on the dust cover. Serial plate mounted on the barrel cluster housing. Tier 4+ military authorization stamp on the magazine coupling. CASELESS 6MM etched near the feed port.
physical_description.condition_typical: Field units show visible heat-bluing progression on barrel clusters from sustained cyclic fire. Polymer shows micro-scratches from equipment contact and sand infiltration in urban environments. Magazine coupling points bear minimal wear despite frequent detachment. Operators often customize rail-mounted accessories, leaving variable coverage patterns.
